trust_rule: Trust Perkins where he transcribes a document verbatim (deeds, decrees, petitions, Board minutes, newspapers): none of his transcriptions in this ledger was contradicted. Do not extend that trust to his summaries of documents he did not transcribe: his statements about a statute (P40), a census count (P41) and a land-claim outcome taken from Bancroft (P33) were all wrong, and a figure he attributes to Bancroft (P29, 2,000 oz) is not in Bancroft's History of California; check those against the document itself. Treat his old-timer hearsay, film and celebrity anecdotes, 'first' superlatives, family-relationship labels, institutional labels (asistencia, Assembly vs Council) and all Indigenous ethnography as unverified until a primary source is found. Spot-check his minor-event dates (typos and year slips are common), and prefer the editor's note where one exists.

ledger.claim: Railroad tunnel (6,964 ft) completed 'in July 1875'
ledger.evidence: Perkins' own 1954 part04 sequences tunnel completion just before the Sept 5, 1876 spike; reynolds part39 places it in July 1876. Reported 2026-10-04: the headings met (holing-through) on Friday night, 14 July 1876, according to ONE report, the LA Herald of 18 Jul 1876, known only at one remove through a reprint (Nathan's rulings, 11:07 and 11:48 PT): Santa Barbara Weekly Press, 22 Jul 1876, p. 2, https://cdnc.ucr.edu/?a=d&d=SBWP18760722.2.44&dliv=none&st=1 , headed 'San Fernando Tunnel. / Los Angeles Herald July 18.': 'On Friday night, the 14th inst., the headings of the San Fernando tunnel were joined. . The tunnel is 6.964 feet long, and has been driven with remarkable rapidity, at more than ordinary expense, …' [page image confirmed at full zoom: the user's full-zoom browser crop perkins-work/zoom/cdnc_zm3/SBWP18760722_tunnel.png, read at letter level by the parent agent, relayed 10:59 PT; '6.964' and the doubled stop are as printed. Scan text (CDNC OCR, checked against the user's screenshot of the CDNC text page, perkins-work/evidence_cdnc3_20261004/): 'On Friday night, the 14th inat, the headings of the San Fernando tunnel werejoined.', credited in the OCR as 'Lon Ancrlri Her«lJ July 18.']. CDNC has neither the LA Herald of 18 Jul nor that of 22 Jul 1876 (direct IDs 404; July 1876 Herald searches empty): library visit list V7. A separate, undated Herald item, not a second source for the date: Morning Press (Santa Barbara), 24 Jul 1876, p. 2 (CDNC MP18760724.2.9), 'THROUGH TO 'FRISCO BY RAIL.': 'The Los Angeles Herald of Saturday publishes the following extract from a private letter of Chas. Crock[er?] to Senator Maclay, giving [ass]urance that rail communication between Los Angeles and San Francisco will be completed within sixty days. The Herald, in making the announcement, throws up its hat and shouts for joy. The extract is as follows: . . . On Friday night last “daylight” shone through the San Fernando tunnel. Within thirty days we expect to be laying track through the tunnel, … and then we'll all go down and see you.' [page image confirmed at full zoom, in part: the user's full-zoom browser crop perkins-work/zoom/cdnc_zm3/MP18760724_whole.png, read at letter level by the parent agent, relayed 10:59 PT; a tooltip covers 'Crock[…] to' and '[ass]urance'; 'Maclay' as printed. Before: "On Friday night last 'daylight' shone through the Ban Fernando tunnel.", a browser session's typed transcription (not read: browser-transcription rule, Nathan 11:07 PT)]. The Morning Press quotes the Herald 'of Saturday' [22 Jul], which quotes an undated private letter, so 'Friday night last' counts from the letter's unknown date: the item cannot date the event, is consistent with the 14th but does not establish it, and gives no support for the 21st (our earlier inference, withdrawn: K20). Both Santa Barbara items are the LA Herald at one remove (second-hand). The 14 July date rests on one Herald report, at one remove; it is not corroborated by a second source. This is the holing-through, not the opening to traffic (the first train came through in August 1876: lwhist; perkins-pico-1958 note f).
